comparator.name: Humanistic Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official bachelor page, checked 2026-09-29, defines a three-year full-time Humanistic Studies programme of 60 ECTS per year and describes the current year-level content. Year one builds foundations in Humanistic Studies, psychology, philosophy, research and normative professionalisation; year two applies history, embodied meaning and citizenship to cases, critical reasoning and intervention design; year three combines a thesis, professional identity, research, guidance and advisory skills with specialization through electives, a minor or study abroad. The official 2025 accreditation report independently confirms the 180-EC degree, its meaning-making, humanisation, research and academic/professional-skills learning lines, and the curriculum revision expanding elective/minor space to 30 EC from 2026-2027. The current public page does not allocate every named activity to individual credits, so the comparator preserves the official 60+60+60 year structure and splits the final year into the documented 30-EC specialization space and the remaining 30-EC thesis/professional core without inventing course titles.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match covers the programme's broad interdisciplinary Humanistic Studies identity, while the generator-backed citizenship and social-cohesion cluster supports one coherent and materially distinct UCR direction. The remaining interests are cross-cutting content already integrated into those programmes rather than separate curricular routes; two alternatives therefore exhaust the defensible candidate set.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Matched explicitly after semantic review: Personal & Professional Development supports the first-year academic, reflective and normative-professional foundation.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Advanced Research Seminar provides a defensible UCR counterpart to the independent-research dimension of the thesis and professionalisation core.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Modern Sociology provides interdisciplinary social-theoretical deepening for analysing societal questions and modernity.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the target's 30-EC specialization, minor or study-abroad space has student-selected content and should not be assigned an invented single-course equivalent.

notes.text: UvH integrates meaning-making and humanisation across dedicated Humanistic Studies learning lines and a thesis/professional sequence. UCR can build a strong interdisciplinary analogue, but it does not award a Humanistic Studies degree or reproduce UvH's exact normative-professional identity and 30-EC specialization structure.
